profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer
profile.summary: Experienced Staff Software Engineer specializing in text understanding and large language models (LLMs) with a proven track record of leading high-impact projects at YouTube. Strong expertise in developing and deploying state-of-the-art machine learning classifiers for ranking, quality, and classification use cases.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Leading text understanding efforts at YouTube with a focus on developing domain-adapted large language models (LLMs) and leveraging state-of-the-art modeling techniques (e.g. distillation, LoRA) to build and improve discriminative classifiers for ranking, quality, and classification use cases across multiple YouTube products (e.g. chat, comments, posts).
• Providing guidance to several junior engineers across a range of projects, including discriminative classifier modeling, leveraging LLMs to provide ground truth labels, and building infrastructure to effectively produce and consume ML model signals.
• Tech lead for horizontal quality efforts for YouTube Community products (comments, chat, @mentions, hashtags). In this capacity, I help drive product roadmaps + strategy and identify gaps in existing approaches/processes.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
• TL for creation-time modeling and infrastructure projects for YouTube Community products (e.g. comments, live chat, hashtags, etc.) worked on by several junior engineers. In this capacity, I led the efforts to launch PaLM 2 derived classifiers for Community applications (e.g. comments low quality classifier).
• Developed a continuous training and deployment system for creation-time ML classifiers that enabled automated monthly releases of classifiers and reduced eng overhead for manual model updates from ~weeks to ~days.
• Paved the path for leveraging ‘LLM as Rater’ labeled training data in a knowledge distillation setup by building a few-shot “LLM as Rater” solution for detecting crypto scam comments and using that LLM Rater to annotate active learning data for the downstream low quality classifier.
• Performed long-term road-mapping for several different project areas, including a state-of-the-art modeling roadmap and Responsibility project roadmap for multiple YouTube Community products (e.g. Hashtags, @mentions).

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Launched multiple CommentBERT-based modeling improvements for live chat and comments low quality classifiers, including multi-head classifiers and the incorporation of active learning training data (derived from uncertainty sampling).
• Lead the cross-team effort to develop serving time filtering and reranking infrastructure for YouTube Comments which powered several launches (e.g. near duplicate comment demotion, racy avatar filtering)
• Oversaw the migration of 10 XL (>500M parameter) ML models and related entity creation-time annotation infrastructure to an internal end-to-end platform for the training, serving, evaluation, and governance of ML models.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
•	Utilized a diffusion-based storytelling algorithm and temporal topic modeling on cyber-security corpora to identify trends and correlations between software vulnerabilities.
•      Developed a comprehensive vulnerability analysis and prediction framework using machine learning models (deep neural network), regression (e.g. linear) and data mining algorithms (e.g. clustering).

company.name: The University of Texas at El Paso

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Implemented and evaluated multiple fairness methodologies (e.g. identity term replacement, data balancing) for the YouTube Live Chat low quality classifier
• Proposed a low tradeoff fairness approach (identity term replacement) for the YouTube live chat low quality classifier and implemented serving time support for the fairness solution.

positions.title: Engineering Practicum Intern
positions.description:
•	Collaborated with another intern to create a system that allows the Guided Search and Discovery team to filter and refine off-topic Play Store search tags with a single click.
•	Designed, implemented, and tested an interface that recursively traverses protocol buffers for data visualization. Initial performance was 15 times faster than the expected 60 minutes and was further improved to less than 15 seconds using distribution and caching.
•	Created an internal feature that displays polished and interactive human evaluation reports for the Guided Search Feature in the Play Store over a 30-day time range
